monthly_review.summary: You've reduced volume significantly this month but increased intensity, shifting HR zone distribution toward higher zones and improving aerobic training effect per run — though average pace slowed and efficiency dipped slightly.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite 36% fewer runs and 35% less distance than last month, your average aerobic training effect rose from 2.7 to 3.0 — indicating higher-quality, more physiologically impactful sessions.

goal_tracker.message: You need 21.4 more km across at least 5 more sessions in the remaining 16 days to match last month’s volume — averaging ~4.3 km per session.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite slower pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.46 to 13.69 m/sec (+0.23), even as average pace slowed (513 → 539 sec/km last month). This suggests better oxygen utilization per unit distance, likely supported by your recent long run (14.1 km at 141 bpm) and consistent Zone 3–4 work.

insights.title: Zone 4 dominance replaced Zone 3 focus
insights.body: Zone 4 time jumped from 15% (June) to 22% (July), while Zone 3 dropped from 31% to 26%. Your July runs show elevated HRs (e.g., 166 bpm on 7/5 over 10 km), suggesting intentional threshold work — but at the expense of foundational Zone 2 endurance.

insights.title: Cadence variability signals fatigue or pacing inconsistency
insights.body: Cadence ranged from 135–154 spm across recent runs, with lowest values (135, 136) occurring on lower-HR easy runs (7/08: 129 bpm; 7/15: 141 bpm) — unusual, as cadence typically rises with effort. This may reflect form breakdown due to cumulative fatigue or under-recovery between sessions.

insights.title: High-intensity density without compensatory recovery
insights.body: You ran 10.0 km at 166 bpm (7/5), then just 0.9 km the next day — insufficient recovery for that level of stress. VO2 max remained stable (39→40), but ground contact time increased on your longest run (319 ms on 7/12 vs. ~300–305 ms on shorter runs), hinting at neuromuscular fatigue.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 5 km Zone 2 effort (HR ≤135 bpm), focusing on cadence ≥148 spm and maintaining ground contact <305 ms
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 2 time dropped from 29% to 27%, and cadence fell below 148 in 3 of 5 recent runs — rebuilding aerobic base and neuromuscular consistency is urgent.

recommendations.action: Insert a full rest day before your next run longer than 8 km — you’ve had only one full rest day since 7/6, and your 14.1 km run showed +14 ms ground contact vs. shorter efforts.
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time increased meaningfully on your longest run (319 ms), signaling reduced leg spring efficiency — likely due to insufficient recovery between high-load sessions.

recommendations.action: Perform 3x1-minute strides post-warmup on your next moderate run (e.g., 6–8 km), focusing on landing midfoot and holding vertical oscillation ≤7.5 cm
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation averaged 7.9 cm recently (vs. 7.6–8.5 range), and stride length dropped to 70.36 cm on your longest run — indicating form decay under fatigue that strides can reinforce.

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize low-HR, high-cadence running to restore Zone 2 volume, reduce ground contact time, and stabilize stride mechanics — balancing the high-intensity emphasis of early July.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 tempo (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥148 spm)
Recovery walk-run hybrid: 3 min walk / 2 min jog x6, focusing on vertical oscillation ≤7.5 cm
